stem: A client with decision-making capacity refuses a recommended treatment after receiving information about the treatment, expected benefits, material risks, and alternatives. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Respect the capable client’s refusal, communicate it to the responsible clinician or team, and document the relevant informed-decision process according to policy.
options.B: Proceed with the treatment because a capable client’s refusal becomes invalid whenever the clinical team believes the expected benefit is substantial.
options.C: Ask a family member to override the refusal because informed refusal applies only when the healthcare team agrees with the client’s choice.
options.D: Document only the words ‘client refused’ and omit the information provided before the decision because that discussion has no relevance to the record.

rationale: CMS hospital informed-consent requirements are intended to ensure that patients or their representatives can make fully informed decisions about care. The Patient's Rights Condition of Participation includes informed decision-making, and the scenario establishes that the capable client received relevant information before refusing. The nurse should respect the decision and follow organizational processes for communication and documentation. A is correct.
educational_objective: Respect an informed treatment refusal by a client with decision-making capacity and complete appropriate communication and documentation processes.
source_document_title: Revisions and Clarifications to Hospital Interpretive Guidelines for Informed Consent
source_locator: Memorandum summary: informed-consent obligations arise under 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2), 482.24(c)(4)(v), and 482.51(b)(2); hospital policy/process/forms must contain information that allows the patient or representative to make fully informed decisions about care.
source_claim_supported: A capable patient who has received the relevant information retains decision-making authority; nursing care should respect the informed decision and follow required communication/documentation processes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7: advocate for client rights and needs; verify the client receives education and consents for care/procedures; initiate/evaluate/update plan of care; maintain legal and ethical practice.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — informed decision-making, client rights and treatment refusal

source_original.stem: A client with decision-making capacity refuses a recommended treatment after receiving information about the treatment, expected benefits, material risks, and alternatives. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Respect the capable client’s refusal, document the relevant information and decision according to policy, and communicate the refusal to the responsible clinician or team.
options.B: Proceed with the treatment because a capable client’s refusal becomes invalid whenever the clinical team believes the expected benefit is substantial.
options.C: Ask a family member to override the refusal because informed refusal applies only when the healthcare team agrees with the client’s choice.
options.D: Document only the words “client refused” and omit the information provided before the decision because that discussion has no relevance to the record.

source_original.rationale: Patient-rights and informed-consent standards recognize the patient’s right to participate in decisions and to give or withhold informed consent. Nursing actions should respect the decision and follow organizational/legal documentation and communication processes.
source_original.source_detail: Hospital Patient Rights CoP — 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2); informed consent policy/process and patient participation in care decisions. CMS QSO-24-10-Hospitals posted 2024-04-01; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Management of Care, printed p.7: advocacy/client rights, prioritization, quality improvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, informed consent, legal scope and plan-of-care activities. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key A and the informed-refusal construct, tightened the wording to respect the capable client's decision while explicitly routing communication/documentation through policy, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: CMS hospital informed-consent guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: CMS QSO-24-10 summary citing 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2) and informed decision-making requirements
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item limits the conclusion to a capable informed client and appropriately separates respect for the decision from organization-specific documentation/communication procedure.

distractor_audit.A: Correct: respects client decision-making and routes required follow-up appropriately.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because expected benefit does not by itself nullify a capable client's informed decision.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because a family member does not override a capable client's decision solely due to disagreement.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the informed-decision context and required documentation process are relevant to the record.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A respects the client's established decision-making capacity and informed choice.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address management of the same refusal; A is determined by client-rights standards.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — client rights, consent, advocacy and legal/ethical practice.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read CMS QSO-24-10, NCSBN Management p.7, all choices, rationale and capacity/information assumptions. A remained uniquely correct.
